chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The keeper of the deposit and the merchant of the goods are two trusted persons."

-(791) 4 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man deposited a trust with another man, who placed it in his neighbor's house, and it was lost. Is it obligatory upon him if he disobeyed his command and took it out of his possession of it? He (peace be upon him) replied: "He is liable for it, if God wills."
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a trustee who disobeys the depositor's instructions regarding the safekeeping of a deposit?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam delineates the fiduciary duty of the 'mu'taman' (trustee), establishing that mere possession does not exempt one from liability if specific conditions of safekeeping are violated. The second report, transmitted from Imam al-Hadi (AS) to Imam al-Hasan al-Mujtaba (AS), clarifies that deviating from the depositor's explicit instruction regarding the deposit's location constitutes a breach of trust, rendering the trustee liable for loss even if the item was not in his direct custody at the time of damage. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on adherence to the depositor's will as a condition for exemption from guarantee (dhaman).
